verification_method: Primary text fetched this session from law.cornell.edu (U.S. Code, FRE) and leg.state.fl.us (Florida Statutes); the Supreme Court case was confirmed via courtlistener.com. Authorities marked verified=true were opened and read; verified=false entries are standard citations recorded for counsel to confirm and are flagged as such.

authorities.title: Registration and civil infringement actions
authorities.requirement: For a 'United States work', no civil action for infringement may be instituted until preregistration or registration of the claim (or refusal of registration). Non-U.S. works are exempt from the registration-to-sue requirement but not from § 412.

authorities.title: Registration as prerequisite to certain remedies for infringement
authorities.requirement: No statutory damages or attorney's fees under §§ 504–505 unless registration precedes infringement, or (for published works) registration is made within three months after first publication.

authorities.title: Infringement of copyright
authorities.requirement: Anyone who violates any exclusive right under § 106 is an infringer; the legal or beneficial owner of an exclusive right may sue subject to § 411.

authorities.title: Remedies: damages and profits
authorities.requirement: Actual damages + infringer's profits (§ 504(b)); or statutory damages of $750–$30,000 per work, up to $150,000 for willful infringement (§ 504(c)). § 504(c)(3) creates a rebuttable presumption of willfulness where materially false contact information was provided to a domain registrar.

authorities.title: Remedies: costs and attorney's fees
authorities.requirement: The court may award full costs and a reasonable attorney's fee to the prevailing party, subject to § 412 timing.

authorities.title: Limitations on liability relating to material online
authorities.requirement: § 512(c)(3) lists the six elements a takedown notice must substantially contain; § 512(d) covers information-location tools; § 512(f) imposes liability for knowing misrepresentation; § 512(h) authorizes a subpoena to identify an infringer, issued by the clerk on a § 512(c)(3) notification, a proposed subpoena, and a sworn declaration.

authorities.title: Patents, plant variety protection, copyrights, mask works, designs, trademarks, and unfair competition
authorities.requirement: United States district courts have exclusive original jurisdiction over civil actions arising under the copyright Act.

authorities.title: Patents and copyrights, mask works, and designs
authorities.requirement: A copyright action may be instituted in the district in which the defendant or the defendant's agent resides or may be found.

authorities.title: Unsworn declarations under penalty of perjury
authorities.requirement: A matter otherwise required to be supported by a sworn affidavit may be supported by an unsworn declaration subscribed as true under penalty of perjury and dated in the statutory form.

authorities.title: Authenticating or identifying evidence
authorities.requirement: The proponent must produce evidence sufficient to support a finding that the item is what it is claimed to be; examples include testimony of a witness with knowledge, Rule 901(b)(1), and evidence about a process or system producing an accurate result, Rule 901(b)(9).

authorities.title: Evidence that is self-authenticating
authorities.requirement: Rule 902(13) allows self-authentication of records generated by an electronic process/system by a qualified person's certification; Rule 902(14) allows self-authentication of data copied from a device/medium/file by a process of digital identification (hash), certified by a qualified person.

authorities.title: Acts subjecting person to jurisdiction of courts of state
authorities.requirement: Florida's long-arm statute reaches a person committing a tortious act within the state (§ 48.193(1)(a)2) and any defendant engaged in substantial and not isolated activity within the state (§ 48.193(2)), subject to due-process limits.

authorities.citation: Fourth Estate Pub. Benefit Corp. v. Wall-Street.com, LLC, 586 U.S. 296 (2019)
authorities.title: Registration is 'made' only when the Copyright Office acts on the application
authorities.requirement: For purposes of § 411(a), registration occurs when the Register of Copyrights registers (or refuses) the claim, not merely when the application is filed.

authorities.title: Registration of claim and issuance of certificate
authorities.note: Standard citation; primary text not re-fetched this session. Counsel to confirm.
authorities.requirement: A certificate of registration made before or within five years after first publication is prima facie evidence of the validity of the copyright and the facts stated in the certificate.

authorities.title: Definitions
authorities.note: Standard citation; primary text not re-fetched this session. Counsel to confirm.
authorities.requirement: Defines 'United States work' by reference to first publication (and related nationality/residence tests), which determines whether § 411(a)'s registration-to-sue requirement applies.

authorities.title: Subject matter of copyright: National origin
authorities.note: Standard citation; primary text not re-fetched this session. Counsel to confirm.
authorities.requirement: Extends protection to works of foreign nationals under Berne and related treaties; foreign authors may enforce U.S. copyrights.

authorities.title: Exclusive rights in copyrighted works
authorities.note: Standard citation; primary text not re-fetched this session. Counsel to confirm.
authorities.requirement: Exclusive rights of reproduction, distribution, and public performance/display — the rights infringed by unauthorized rehosting.

authorities.title: Subpoena
authorities.note: Standard citation; primary text not re-fetched this session. Counsel to confirm.
authorities.requirement: Governs third-party subpoenas in federal litigation (documents, deposition, inspection); § 512(h) and Rule 45 are the mechanisms to identify the infringer.

authorities.title: Injunctions and restraining orders
authorities.note: Standard citation; primary text not re-fetched this session. Counsel to confirm.
authorities.requirement: Governs temporary restraining orders and preliminary injunctions to restrain ongoing infringement.

authorities.title: Failure to make disclosures or to cooperate in discovery
authorities.note: Standard citation; primary text not re-fetched this session. Counsel to confirm.
authorities.requirement: Addresses sanctions for failure to preserve electronically stored information; supports the need for documented preservation of the rehosted copies.

authorities.citation: Lorraine v. Markel Am. Ins. Co., 241 F.R.D. 534 (D. Md. 2007)
authorities.title: Authentication of electronically stored information
authorities.note: Landmark ESI-authentication opinion; citation standard. Counsel to confirm.
authorities.requirement: Sets out the authentication/relevance/hearsay/best-evidence analysis for electronic evidence, including web pages and digital records.

authorities.citation: United States v. Bansal, 663 F.3d 634 (3d Cir. 2011)
authorities.title: Authentication of web page printouts
authorities.requirement: Web-page printouts may be authenticated by distinctive characteristics and circumstantial evidence under Rule 901(b)(4).

authorities.citation: Mitchell Bros. Film Grp. v. Cinema Adult Theater, 604 F.2d 852 (5th Cir. 1979)
authorities.title: Obscene works are copyrightable
authorities.note: Standard citation. Counsel to confirm. (See also Jartech, Inc. v. Clancy, 666 F.2d 403 (9th Cir. 1982).)
authorities.requirement: Content's adult/obscene nature is not a defense to copyright infringement; obscenity does not defeat copyrightability.

authorities.title: Personal jurisdiction from intentional conduct aimed at the forum
authorities.requirement: Intentional, forum-targeted conduct can support personal jurisdiction (effects test).

authorities.title: Minimum contacts must arise from the defendant's own contacts with the forum
authorities.requirement: Limits personal jurisdiction; the defendant's own contacts with the forum state must be the basis, not merely the plaintiff's residence.

authorities.citation: Zubulake v. UBS Warburg LLC, 220 F.R.D. 212 (S.D.N.Y. 2003)
authorities.title: Duty to preserve relevant evidence
authorities.note: Standard citation (the Zubulake line). Counsel to confirm.
authorities.requirement: Once litigation is reasonably anticipated, a party must preserve relevant evidence; informs our preservation obligations and posture.

authorities.citation: Feist Publ'ns, Inc. v. Rural Tel. Serv. Co., 499 U.S. 340 (1991)
authorities.title: Originality requirement
authorities.requirement: Copyright requires a modicum of originality; supports the authorship/ownership showing for the works.
